entry.title: Ubisoft Details Rendering Pipeline for Assassin's Creed Shadows
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com | source

During a GDC 2025 presentation, Technical Architect Nicolas Lopez outlined the rendering advancements in Assassin's Creed Shadows and the evolution of the Anvil engine. The engine has transitioned to a monorepo architecture to streamline development and features enhanced scalability to support massive, systemic open worlds.

The architecture relies on a GPU-driven pipeline and a specialized "Database" system for efficient data sharing between the CPU and GPU. Performance across vast environments is maintained through a hierarchy of LOD techniques, including point clouds for mass imposter rendering and a micro-polygon geometry pipeline for efficient rasterization.

entry.title: Game Designers Share Personal Design Rules at GDC 2015
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com | source

In this GDC 2015 session, Richard Rouse III explores the subjective "rules" and "tricks" that experienced game designers use to shape their creative processes. The discussion highlights that effective design principles are often personal methodologies rather than universal mandates.

Laurelyn McWills demonstrates how to bridge the gap between technical systems and player emotion by treating human needs as systemic requirements. She argues that incorporating emotional drivers, such as the need for social connection or a sense of progress, allows for the creation of "experiential core loops" that deepen immersion and player engagement.

entry.title: Red Hook Studios Explains Art-Led Procedural Generation for Darkest Dungeon 2
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com | source

Red Hook Studios' Darkest Dungeon 2 utilizes an art-led procedural generation system to balance a specific visual style with gameplay replayability. To avoid the high labor costs and visual repetition of an initial "sequential plate" approach, the development team transitioned to a modular hex-based grid system.

This system generates interconnected nodes and branching paths that facilitate strategic decision-making. By using smaller tiles, the developers were able to increase visual variety and maintain the game's signature ink-heavy, painterly aesthetic across different biomes.

entry.title: Adam Russell Discusses Marginal Gains in LEGO Horizon Adventures
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com | source

Studio Gobo lead designer Adam Russell applies the "marginal gains" philosophy to the development of LEGO Horizon Adventures, demonstrating how small, incremental improvements compound to create significant impact. Drawing parallels to the success of British cycling, the approach involves identifying and optimizing minor friction points in workflows, technical tools, and player features.

Implementation of these gains included the development of custom editor icons for enemy spawns, ledge grab visualizations, and automated validation checks for combat encounters. On the product side, improvements focused on accessibility, navigation via waypoint markers, and the inclusion of diverse minifigures to enhance the overall player experience.

entry.title: Owen Mahoney Identifies Four Distinct Gaming Sub-Industries
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com

The gaming industry is comprised of four distinct sectors: single-player casual, single-player core, mobile/casual live service, and core live service. The mobile and casual live service market functions as a math-driven business focused on user acquisition and lifetime value via gacha mechanics, whereas core PC and console markets rely on cosmetic sales and gameplay-integrated randomness.

This divergence in monetization necessitates different company structures and design philosophies. While math-based mechanics drive success in mobile gaming, the core audience generally requires a focus on cosmetic items and gameplay-focused randomness to maintain engagement.

entry.title: Steam's 2024 Demo Updates and Their Impact on Game Visibility
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com | source

Valve's "Great Steam Demo Update 2024" has introduced significant changes to how game demos function on Steam, including visibility in the "New & Trending" section and the ability to host separate store pages. These updates allow demos to act as more effective marketing tools by enabling user reviews and direct notification emails to players who have wishlisted the demo.

Effective deployment involves a tiered approach: using frequent playtests to build momentum, coordinating demo launches with streaming influencers and industry festivals, and reserving Steam NextFest as a final promotional milestone. This strategy aims to maximize algorithmic visibility and convert high engagement during demo periods into long-term wishlist growth and revenue.

entry.content:

The studio is also developing upcoming titles for platforms including Netflix.

entry.title: Sunfall Interactive Discusses Technical Development of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com

The production of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 relied on a programming team of only four members who implemented 95% of core gameplay logic via Unreal Engine Blueprints. This strategy empowered designers to create content independently and facilitated rapid iteration by avoiding the stability and compilation overhead typical of C++. This workflow allowed the small team to support a high volume of content across semi-open environments and turn-based combat systems.

Development followed a "vanilla first" philosophy, prioritizing native engine features and third-party plugins over bespoke engine tools to maximize efficiency. While C++ was reserved for performance-critical tasks, platform-specific code, and core engine modifications, the studio implemented a dedicated build farm to manage the extended packaging times caused by the heavy reliance on visual scripting.

entry.title: OpenTIE Reimplementation of Star Wars: TIE Fighter for Windows, macOS, and Linux
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | github.com | hacker news

OpenTIE is an open-source reimplementation of Star Wars: TIE Fighter designed for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It runs original game data natively and allows users to combine assets from the 1995 Collector's CD-ROM and the 1998 Windows release, such as the 1995 adaptive iMUSE soundtrack and menus with the 1998 flight simulation.

Modernization features include ambient occlusion, bloom, HDR output, and AMD FidelityFX FSR 3.1.4 upscaling. The software supports high-refresh-rate displays up to 240 Hz and provides compatibility for modern gamepads and joysticks.

entry.title: Experimental NVIDIA DLSS 5 Mod Active in Multiple Games
entry.content:
Techmeme | videocardz.com

Modders have successfully integrated an experimental NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering library into more than a dozen games, including Cyberpunk 2077, Red Dead Redemption 2, and Grand Theft Auto V. The implementation utilizes a DLL discovered in the NBA 2K27 early access build and connects it to various rendering pipelines using the RenoDX modding framework, allowing the tech to run in titles without native support.

Current tests indicate a heavy performance penalty, with some scenarios seeing frame rates drop by nearly 50% on RTX 50-series hardware. While NVIDIA's official implementation is expected to include specialized controls for color grading and lighting intensity, these community mods serve as an unoptimized demonstration of the unreleased technology.
